why: A 180-minute neorealist "portrait of childhood stolen by war" in postwar Tokyo, unsentimental about "abandonment, abused childhoods," from an established Japanese auteur with Koji Yakusho.

title: Head to Head
why: A Persian-language "film within a film" that makes "brilliant use of humour" to satirize male directors' portrayal of women and Iranian censorship, mockery rising alongside real political weight.

title: I Am Mario
why: Naturalistic Mexican debut about a pregnant trans man "completely cornered by life," dignified and slow-burning social drama with transphobic language and explicit sex.

title: Idda
why: "Languidly mysterious portrait" of a simmering female friendship climbing Etna, understated violence and a devastating loss, in Italian with a meandering, portentous camera.

title: In Conversation With... Andrew Scott
why: A live on-stage career conversation with Andrew Scott, exploring "the remarkable range of Scott's career" — nonfiction talk event, no narrative form.

title: In Conversation With... Chris Rock
why: A live onstage talk with Chris Rock about his "multi-faceted career" — nonfiction event in a comic register, no narrative form.

title: Krux
why: WWII village atrocity drama of "moral collapse, societal panic" with "haunting visuals," brutal historical violence, German-language debut running 122 minutes.

title: Memories of a Forest
why: Quiet German-language rural family drama about inheritance and duty, a "stunning debut" of landscape and laconic feeling rather than incident.

title: Nosotros
why: A quiet, restrained Guatemalan debut of "nuance, restraint, and clarity" about migration, loneliness, and a fragile trans romance amid homophobic hostility.

title: On Behalf of My Son
why: A 178-minute Brazilian "meditation on guilt, grief" told "with remarkable feeling and restraint," following a mother seeking forgiveness from victims' families.

title: Seventeen
why: Ticking-clock naturalist drama of three queer Indigenous sex workers over 17 hours in "gritty downtown Vancouver," heavy and conventional in form, mostly English with some Cree.

title: Silenced Nights
why: A "bleak drama" of Manila drug-war killings shot cinéma vérité in the Happyland slum, driven by an investigation that keeps hitting "brick walls."

title: Sisters
why: Spanish/Basque family drama of sexual assault and trial with "observational approach" and "measured sadness" — heavy, deliberate, subtitled, conventionally told.

title: Strong Son
why: Character-driven debut about a bodybuilder "trapped in a quagmire of anxiety and insecurity" caregiving for his father, with "teary public breakdowns" and Sikh family dynamics, largely English with some Punjabi.

title: The Daughters of Abraham
why: Naturalistic French-language debut about estranged Muslim and Jewish friends whose reunion is broken by "an unexpected tragedy" — an "incisive study of faith and gender" called "propulsive" but essentially intimate drama.

title: The Fortunate Isles
why: A "restrained epic of colonial regret" with "tactile camera and uniquely portentous style" — slow, poetic, formally elevated period drama of enslavement and drought, in Spanish/Arabic.

title: The World Before
why: Quiet Korean island coming-of-age where "the camera often remains still and attentive" and drama is found in the everyday, tender and bittersweet across 145 minutes.

title: We Are Born Good
why: An "escalating feud" comedy-drama with "narrative momentum" and humour, set among debt-crushed Hong Kongers "worn down by grief, anger, and exhaustion."

title: What Lies Between Us
why: A "provocative and gripping" Danish moral drama about mothers and a sexual assault accusation, "expertly paced" and conventionally told, with heavy themes and strong performances.

title: Wild Wild East
why: "A suspenseful western meets wartime noir" set in 1943 occupied Poland, a web of betrayal and greed among traumatized villagers and Nazi authorities, in Polish/German/Ukrainian at 135 min.

title: Zjili: A Story of Sisterhood and The Burdens of Excess
why: Social-realist Ghanaian drama of kayayei porters told "without sensationalism or artifice," 149 min in Dagbani/Twi, grounded in research and dedicated to a woman who died under a load.

title: A Girl Unknown
why: A "quiet, painful, yet ultimately hopeful coming-of-age story" in chapters across 158 minutes, tracing abandonment and displacement with restrained performances in Chinese.

title: After Elena
why: A "gentle, non-judgmental" Spanish-language family grief drama that "doesn't wallow in heaviness," finding richness in small gestures with "humour, melancholy," and "absurd situations."

title: Ah Girl
why: Autobiographical 1990s Singapore childhood drama with "soft cinematography" and "delicate, hazy" dreamy sequences, mundane detail and "bittersweet déjà vu" over painful family rupture.

title: Ashes
why: A "mature and nuanced" immigrant drama of displacement and "toughest trials" in Spanish/Catalan, conventionally told with heavy emotional toll.

title: Babies
why: A star-studded, "relatable, hilarious, and wise" mainstream ensemble comedy about whether to have kids — conventional, big-hearted, low stakes.

title: Ben'Imana
why: Rwandan gacaca-court drama on genocide trauma and forced motherhood, "powerful intergenerational narrative" in Kinyarwanda, Caméra d'Or winner at 131 min.

title: Congo Boy
why: Handheld "immediacy" and rap-driven "singular rhythms" energize a hustling refugee teen's story in Sango/French/Lingala, weighty but "inspiring" with "colossal heart."

title: Eklipse
why: "Poetic realism" coming-of-age in rural 1999 Austria, German-language, with VHS footage blending reality and fiction and a father's hidden illness driving quiet heaviness.

title: Elephants in the Fog
why: "Fierce but tender debut" with non-actors, "exquisitely rendered images of the verdant setting" and a slow tension between tradition and modernity in a Nepali third-gender community.

title: Evil Genius
why: True-crime dramatization "reminiscent of the Coen Brothers at their most cunningly funny," "brimming with bloodshed, betrayals," with a Gala star cast and non-linear backtracking structure.

title: Four Seasons in Java
why: Andini's "most ambitious yet" 167-minute female-centred drama on sexual violence, blending fantasy and "breathtaking visuals" with "deep metaphors," demanding and bleak.

title: Furies
why: A 164-minute Arabic-language Beirut heist thriller with "fast-paced editing" and a "thrilling race against the clock," rooted in the bleak reality of Lebanon's banking collapse.

title: Future Tense
why: A "thrilling journey through time" sci-fi from Jenna Cato Bass, mixing climate-collapse dread and colonial violence with romance, partly in Xhosa and Afrikaans.

title: Girl Group
why: Crowd-pleasing musical comedy with a "hilarious cast" and "fantastic soundtrack," conventional mentor-redemption arc for a "jaded pop-star burnout."

title: God Bless You, Mr Kopu
why: "Sharp social satire" with "swagger of late-1970s hustler and action cinema" that builds into a "propulsive thriller," a dark comedy in mostly English with Tongan cultural specificity.

title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
why: A "stylized melange of melodrama and fantasia" about grief in Tokyo — quirky, fleet-footed and playful with fantasy interludes (a colossal crow, Dirty Dancing), largely Japanese/Spanish-language at 151 min.

title: Iron Boy
why: Hand-painted animated coming-of-age memoir, "beautiful and whimsical," French-language Cannes Special Jury Prize winner from an ex-Pixar animator.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils
why: "Feverish," transgressive Russell provocation staging "mass hysteria, torture, and exorcism as history, horror, and political allegory" in baroque excess with body horror.

title: Kissed
why: "Ethereal atmosphere" akin to Crash and Exotica, a dreamy, trance-like drama of necrophilia that balances "reality and fantasy" rather than playing as horror.

title: L'AUTRE
why: A "darkly comedic thriller about a mind and body in peril," confined to a hospital room but "visceral, sometimes harrowing" with drug-addled unreality and "bristling energy."

title: La Gradiva
why: A 175-minute French-Italian ensemble coming-of-age film in Pompeii balancing "visual poetry with an intellectual rigour" and a "documentary-like approach to shooting."

title: Light Pillar
why: "Melancholic, visually audacious meditation on alienation" with hand-drawn animation for reality and live action for VR — formally daring, quietly immersive, slow and wistful.

title: Long Long Night
why: "Radiant animation" fable of a rhino and penguin, "alternating between mirth and profound loss" with poachers and tragedy, Korean-language Centrepiece debut.

title: Love is the monster
why: "Bold tropical dystopian" kidnapping thriller "mixing elements of genre storytelling," tense and "deeply unsettling" vision of inequality, in Spanish with Paulina García.

title: Muyi
why: A "charming, imaginative, and visually stunning" French-language animated coming-of-age fable set in China, with whimsical touches like "a vegetarian tiger and a magical guide."

title: Onwards and Sideways
why: Conventional British illness dramedy with "heartache, laughter, and hard-won connection" — sober look at degenerative disease leavened by irreverent humour, at a comfortable Gala 140 minutes.

title: Our Loves
why: A 147-minute Hebrew/Arabic "dramatic network narrative" of interwoven personal griefs that turns to catastrophe and communal survival, "moving and profound" rather than kinetic.

title: Pretenders
why: Conventional archival-and-interview music doc on Chrissie Hynde, "tough, stylish" with "thrilling performance footage" and a tragedy at its centre.

title: Soumsoum, The Night of the Stars
why: Haroun's Ennedi-set tale of an ostracized visionary girl takes "a realistic approach to the fantasy genre," contemplative and mythic, in Arabic and French, with heavy themes of exclusion and the dead.

title: The Difficult Bride
why: Bengali-language Centrepiece body-horror-inflected drama "awash in striking images" of catfish, snakes, and things moving under skin, dwelling on a bride's asphyxiating pressures rather than plot momentum.

title: The Dreamed Adventure
why: A 194-minute Bulgarian-language "masterful slow-burn" of smuggling and memory from Grisebach, Cannes Jury Prize winner, with crime plot points as "blips in something bigger and more nebulous."

title: The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd
why: "Psychologically rich prison story about crime, punishment, and love" in Oklahoma, 151 min of abusive marriage and incarceration — heavy, conventional character drama with star performances.

title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
why: "Low-key crime drama" with a "meditation on changing times" in the character-driven 1970s New Hollywood mode, carried by Turturro's charm.

title: The Violinist
why: Sweeping animated wartime romance spanning eight decades, "an emotional ride, traversing loss, remembrance, resilience," at 144 min with Annecy's Cristal top prize.

title: The bovine with the curved horns
why: Magical-realist child's-eye view of paramilitary terror in the Ciénaga Grande, with non-professional cast, myth and "cadence of rhythms of daily life," unfolding "poetically" in nuanced black-and-white.

title: Toy Gun Bandit
why: "Wildly energetic" Quebec crime comedy with "escalating mayhem" and "restless, reckless vitality," balanced by warmth and a drug-addiction downward trajectory.

title: Up Against It
why: "Wickedly clever comedy" and "inventive spin on the screwball comedy" built around a child's leukemia, star-driven Gala at 152 minutes.

title: We Are All Strangers
why: Anthony Chen's 187-minute closing chapter of his Growing Up trilogy: a slow, humanist family drama of "emotional journey and growing pains" and class divides, largely in Mandarin.

title: Where the River Begins
why: "Gritty" naturalist migration drama with non-professional Indigenous cast, displacement and paramilitary violence, but "more poetic and more poignant" than urgent thriller.

title: Ancestors
why: "Mesmerizing journey through a dreamlike 1980s London" where "memory and longing become impossible to separate" — a slow, visionary AIDS-legacy elegy, "heartbreaking without ever surrendering to despair."

title: Magazine
why: A talky, observational debut about a poet intern's "sentimental education" in the pre-#MeToo literary scene — conventional narrative, socially barbed, with a longish 135-minute runtime.

title: Masc
why: "Striking, deeply original debut" structured in five chapters shot over a year, an observational portrait "not around crisis or coming out" but subtler identity work, with an "unexpected finale" beyond words.

title: Purgatory
why: A "charming, gentle, and funny" 1980s coming-of-age dramedy in the Lady Bird/Eighth Grade mode, conventional in form with a 134-min runtime.

title: Salvation
why: Assured Scottish debut about a delusional would-be life coach — social-realist character study we "cringe at" with "unnerving depth," lightly comic but sincere and desperate.

title: Voices
why: Single-location "noir-ish" 1967 Detroit musical about a desperate con, with "infectious musical reveries" lifting the register from its claustrophobic, corrupting-fame darkness.

title: Back in Black
why: A "deliciously macabre black comedy" and "sabre-toothed satire" with Walken's foul-mouthed mortician and small-town murder "accidents" — conventional narrative, huge comic register, mild genre darkness.

title: How We Stand
why: A "riveting drama of sisters" shaped by Indigenous relocation policy, heavy with trauma and sexual violence but lifted by magic realism and "a dose of humour" sending up Hollywood westerns.

title: Lemonade
why: Tender social-realist debut about an Irish care leaver that finds "warmth, humour, romance, and gentle beauty in everyday moments" rather than grimness, observational at 142 minutes with Barry Keoghan grounding it.

title: Neverman
why: A "cold, austere, and threatening institution" holds a trans elder with worsening Alzheimer's, told in flashbacks — heavy, largely conventional drama with a faint thriller edge.

title: Smudge the Blades
why: A "dramedy" underdog hockey movie in the Bad News Bears mould, "grittier and more dramatic" with "high-energy hockey play" and laughs, set on a Northern Alberta reserve.

title: Sunburn
why: A "loose, funny" hang-out coming-of-age film in the spirit of Dazed and Confused, sweaty and vibrant but plotless and low-stakes.

title: Tangles
why: Hand-drawn 2D animated Alzheimer's memoir, "deeply moving" with heavy material balanced by comic voice cast levity.

title: The Betrayers
why: "Gripping and elegant" literary adaptation of moral/political drama in Yalta, largely English but steeped in Soviet-Israeli history, talky and character-driven rather than kinetic.

title: The Surgeon
why: A "pulse-pounding" "scalp 'em up" with Michelle Yeoh, breathless fight scenes, extreme violence and needle drops — pure genre blockbuster with conventional form.

title: Trash Mountain
why: "Funny, wise" homecoming comedy that "overflows with irreverence and tenderness" — conventional indie dramedy with real grief underneath.

title: Alice
why: A "sweeping series" period biopic of Alice Guy-Blaché in La Belle Époque Paris, conventional prestige narrative in French with Bérénice Bejo.

title: Blindspot Berlin
why: "A compelling procedural thriller" reconstructing the 2016 Breitscheidplatz attack, "unflinching" and heavy with surveillance and radicalization, in German/Arabic/Turkish.

title: Oxygen Masks Will (Not) Drop Automatically
why: 1980s Brazilian AIDS drama where "joy and dread were intertwined" — neon club vibrancy against stigma and death, conventional narrative in Portuguese at 140 min.

title: YAGA
why: A Baba Yaga-inflected small-town detective story that "blends elements of horror and whodunnit," with wry banter and a "preternatural air" of lurking monstrosity.

title: American Hostage
why: Fact-based hostage stand-off thriller about radio ethics, "murky boundaries between participant and observer," conventional Primetime series with tense but talk-driven procedural energy.

title: Below
why: Newfoundland family drama fused with "the chilly depths of marine monstrousness" — conventional creature-feature storytelling balancing warmth and dread.

title: Crystal Lake
why: A24 Friday the 13th origin series: "a moving portrait of a mother consumed with grief" plus "a very high body count" and "a bloody good time."

title: Slow Horses
why: TV spy thriller episodes with "propulsive energy and dark humour," "quick-witted and always entertaining ride" through espionage.

title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
why: Jude's "slapstick skewering of modern-day slavery" in Wavelengths — a formally provocative, talky French/Romanian satire that is also "surprisingly tender."

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
why: A "rapturous living archive" of Harlem Renaissance luminaries shot on multiple 16mm cameras at a 1972 party, structureless and conversational with "humour, fervour... and not a bit of melancholy."

title: Growth of the Soil
why: A 185-minute "fervently realistic" period epic of homesteading hardship in northern Norway, played with "grace and gravity" in conventional narrative form.

title: Making Waves With... Hudson Williams
why: Not a film but an "intimate conversation" with actor Hudson Williams for TIFF Next Wave, a talk-format event with no cinematic form of its own.

title: Pelechian Project
why: Wordless "visually and musically maximalist" montage documentaries with "passages of pure exhilaration," each "a harrowing ode to humanity" — formally radical nonfiction, newly restored.

title: In Conversation With... Lee Min-ho
why: A live onstage career conversation with "global Hallyu icon Lee Min-ho" — not a film at all, closest to nonfiction talk with Korean-language cultural context.

screenings.v: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
screenings.r: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

title: In Conversation With... Rachel Morrison
why: Live onstage conversation with Oscar-nominated cinematographer-director Rachel Morrison about her "remarkable journey" — nonfiction talk, no dramatic form, craft-focused rather than heavy or genre.

title: At Night
why: Wavelengths debut feature of "poetic, collaborative autofiction" that "boldly transcends traditional narrative," shifting between narrative, documentary, and dream on 16mm, melancholic and multilingual.

title: Double Freedom
why: Alonso's Wavelengths echo of La libertad, a slow 35mm day-in-the-life with non-professional actors, "invigorating rejection of traditional narrative" and a quietly moving meditation on care and freedom.

title: Everything Else is Noise
why: A "sly, self-reflexive comedy of manners and mishaps" in Wavelengths, chamber-piece structure with "inspiring economy of form" and Lubitschian light touch, in Spanish at 101 minutes.

title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges
why: A 370-minute Wavelengths essay-film by La Flor's Llinás that "blurs the line between the real and the invented," digressive, erudite, playful, and enormously demanding.

title: London
why: An "experimental road movie" of static car conversations shot with vintage rear-projection, 150 min of "existential colloquy" in German inspired by James Benning.

title: My Wife Cries
why: Schanelec's "austere and solemn" 35mm elegy of "emotional distance and anguish," with "painterly still life compositions" and eccentric intrusions, is deep-contemplative art cinema in German.

title: Nobody's Violence
why: Wavelengths Côté euthanasia dystopia that "shape-shifts from sci-fi parable to conspiracy thriller to Buñuelian comedy" with "restless, relentless vitality" across 148 French-language minutes.

title: REDEFINED | Short Film Showcase
why: Five short personal-storytelling works from Canadian and Indigenous filmmakers exploring "culture, belonging, identity, and sovereign(ties)," suggesting essayistic, largely documentary-leaning form.

title: Short Cuts 2026 / Strange Cuts
why: No substantive note; inferred from a Short Cuts shorts programme titled "Strange Cuts," suggesting genre-tinged, formally offbeat work of varied origin.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 01
why: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no content; placements are Short Cuts programme priors — mixed shorts, some formal play and international work.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 02
why: Note is only TIFF's boilerplate mission statement, so placement rests entirely on the Short Cuts prior: a mixed 131-min shorts block of varied tone and language.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 03
why: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no film detail; placements are generic Short Cuts averages — mixed forms, some subtitled work, anthology of varied registers.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 04
why: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no content; placements are generic Short Cuts averages — mixed-form shorts anthology at 130 min.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 05
why: Note is boilerplate mission text with no film detail; placements default to Short Cuts shorts-programme averages of mixed tone and moderate formal play.

title: Short Cuts 2026 Programme 06
why: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no film detail; placed at neutral defaults for a mixed Short Cuts anthology programme, which tends toward mild formal play and varied language.

title: The Black Box is Orange
why: A "multimodal, autobiographical essay film" in 10 stylistically distinct chapters with hand-processed 16mm and contrapuntal sound, reckoning with the Nakba, occupation, and complicit memory.

title: The Remotes
why: "Spacious and elliptical" 183-min Wavelengths hybrid of sci-fi/noir procedural, hypnotic night drives and "post-colonial grief" in Tagalog.

title: Wavelengths 1: House and Home
why: Wavelengths shorts programme of "poetic, tactile" essay films on shelter and memory, mixing archival rumination with "resolutely incensed" political chronicle.

title: Wavelengths 2: This Suffocating Now
why: Wavelengths shorts programme of essay films and in-camera experiments — Tafakory's "layered, lucid essay film," Kosugi's 8mm lyricism, night-vision strolls, and a "visceral" political accusation.

title: Wavelengths 3: Time and Tide
why: Wavelengths shorts programme of 65mm formalism, Baroque illusionism, archival 8mm Roma footage and a Duras/Conrad-inspired essay — avowedly experimental and contemplative.

title: Wavelengths: Anoushahpour/Aljafari
why: Two "unhurried" Wavelengths essay-documentaries on memory and imagination, one Kurdish-village embroidery portrait, one "understated" observational study of Masao Adachi's passport attempt.
